cases.sentence: На ___ стола разговор всё более и более оживлялся.
cases.explain: «мужском конце» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.
cases.translation: At the men’s end of the table the talk grew more and more animated. The colonel told them that the declaration of war had already appeared in Petersburg and that a copy, which he had himself seen, had that day been forwarded by courier to the commander in chief.

cases.sentence: И с свойственною ему непогрешимою, официальною памятью он повторил ___ манифеста...
cases.explain: «вступительные слова» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Then with the unerring official memory that characterized him he repeated from the opening words of the manifesto: … and the wish, which constitutes the Emperor’s sole and absolute aim—to establish peace in Europe on firm foundations—has now decided him to despatch part of the army abroad and to create a new condition for the attainment of that purpose.

cases.sentence: «и желание, единственную и непременную цель государя составляющее: водворить в Европе на ___ мир — решили его двинуть ныне часть войска за границу и сделать к достижению намерения сего новые усилия».
cases.explain: «прочных основаниях» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Then with the unerring official memory that characterized him he repeated from the opening words of the manifesto: … and the wish, which constitutes the Emperor’s sole and absolute aim—to establish peace in Europe on firm foundations—has now decided him to despatch part of the army abroad and to create a new condition for the attainment of that purpose.

cases.explain: «старые гусары» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Ve must vight to the last tr-r-op of our plood!” said the colonel, thumping the table; “and ve must tie for our Emperor, and zen all vill pe vell. And ve must discuss it as little as po-o-ossible” … he dwelt particularly on the word possible … “as po-o-ossible,” he ended, again turning to the count. “Zat is how ve old hussars look at it, and zere’s an end of it! And how do you, a young man and a young hussar, how do you judge of it?” he added, addressing Nikoláy, who when he heard that the war was being discussed had turned from his partner with eyes and ears intent on the colonel.

cases.sentence: — Настоящэй гусар, ___, — крикнул полковник, ударив опять по столу.
cases.explain: «молодой человэк» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “The young man’s a real hussar!” shouted the colonel, again thumping the table.

cases.sentence: На всё воля Божья: и на печи лежа умрешь, и в сражении Бог помилует, — прозвучал без всякого усилия, с того конца стола ___ Марьи Дмитриевны.
cases.explain: «густой голос» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “I have four sons in the army but still I don’t fret. It is all in God’s hands. You may die in your bed or God may spare you in a battle,” replied Márya Dmítrievna’s deep voice, which easily carried the whole length of the table.

cases.sentence: — А вот не спросишь, — говорил ___ Наташе, — а вот не спросишь!
cases.explain: «маленький брат» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “You won’t ask,” Natásha’s little brother was saying; “I know you won’t ask!”

cases.explain: «детски-грудной голос» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Mamma!” rang out the clear contralto notes of her childish voice, audible the whole length of the table.

cases.explain: «толстым пальцем» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: The countess tried to frown, but could not. Márya Dmítrievna shook her fat finger.

cases.sentence: — Вот и спросила, — прошептала Наташа ___ и Пьеру, на которого она опять взглянула.
cases.explain: «маленькому брату» — the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: “You see! I have asked,” whispered Natásha to her little brother and to Pierre, glancing at him again.

cases.sentence: Опять забегали официанты, загремели стулья, и в том же порядке, но с более ___, гости вернулись в гостиную и кабинет графа.
cases.explain: «красными лицами» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Natásha only desisted when she had been told that there would be pineapple ice. Before the ices, champagne was served round. The band again struck up, the count and countess kissed, and the guests, leaving their seats, went up to “congratulate” the countess, and reached across the table to clink glasses with the count, with the children, and with one another. Again the footmen rushed about, chairs scraped, and in the same order in which they had entered but with redder faces, the guests returned to the drawing room and to the count’s study.
